chunks: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Abi Hamza. He said: Dawud b. Kathir al-Raqqi informed me. He said: I heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever wishes that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, lighten for him the pangs of death, let him maintain his kinship ties and be dutiful to his parents; for when he does so, Allah will ease for him the pangs of death, and he will never be afflicted with poverty in his life.

key_terms.بَارًّا: dutiful/righteous toward — particularly used for dutiful behavior toward parents (birr al-walidayn)
key_terms.سَكَرَاتِ الْمَوْتِ: pangs/agonies of death — the intense spiritual and physical suffering at the moment of dying
key_terms.قَرَابَة: kinship, relatives — blood relations beyond the immediate family
key_terms.وَصُولاً: one who maintains/upholds ties — actively maintaining kinship relations (silat al-rahim)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about easing the pangs of death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that maintaining kinship ties (silat al-rahim) and being dutiful to parents (birr al-walidayn) brings two divine rewards: ease at the time of death and freedom from poverty throughout life. This teaching was addressed to the early Shia community who faced social pressures that sometimes severed family ties; the Imam reminded them that proper family relations are not merely social etiquette but have eschatological consequences. The original audience would have understood 'pangs of death' (sakarat al-mawt) as referring to the spiritual and physical distress at the moment of dying, which Islamic tradition holds can be mitigated by righteous deeds.
